Svirzh New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Svirzh, Ukraine

Demolished. No founding date survives, though the cemetery appears on 19th- and 20th-century maps; it was presumably demolished after WWII. Jews are first mentioned in Svirzh in 1563; the community took particular pride in a legendary multi-story menorah housed in its local synagogue. Stratin Hasidism predominated, though many Jews emigrated to the US in the late 19th century. Population reached 381 (20%) by 1880, settling at 352 (15%) by 1900. The Wehrmacht occupied Svirzh in late July 1941; in November 1942, the Jewish population was expelled to the ghettos of Bibrka and Peremyshlyany.
